headline: デザイン is the English word “design” in katakana.
飢える came from the classical verb 飢う (uu), with a sound path from /uwu/ to /ueru/.
ポケット is the English word “pocket” in katakana.
世話 is believed to derive from 忙しい (sewashii, “busy”), and its kanji are ateji.
ダンス is borrowed from English “dance”.
そんな is a contraction of その様な (sono yō na).
ジーンズ is the English word “jeans” in katakana.
硬い, “hard, firm, solid”, is from Old Japanese and first attested in the Kojiki of 712 CE.
ママ is the English word “mama” in katakana.
デザート is borrowed from English “dessert”.
来, “next ~”, comes from Middle Chinese 來 (MC loj).
テンポ comes from Italian “tempo”.
願う is a compound of 祈が (nega) and the auxiliary ふ (fu), which indicates repetition or ongoing state.
スチュワーデス is borrowed from English “stewardess”.
象, “elephant”, is a goon reading, so likely the initial borrowing from Middle Chinese.
プレゼント, “present, gift”, is borrowed from English “present” and first attested in the 1900s.
温まる is built from あたた, the root of 暖か (“warm”), plus まる (“to become (an adjective), -en”).
タクシー is borrowed from English “taxi”.
ネクタイ is the English word “necktie” in katakana.
鉢, “a bowl, a pot”, is shortened from 缽多羅 (“monk's alms bowl”), a transcription of Sanskrit pātra.
ピンク is borrowed from English “pink”.
あちら is built from the archaic あち plus 等 (ra), which the source glosses “about; around; approximately”.
シリーズ is the English word “series” in katakana.
焚く is speculatively linked to Korean 타다 (tada), but the source says that poses issues.
ブレーキ is the English word “brake” in katakana.
オートメーション is the English word “automation” in katakana.
表す is derived as the verb form of 露 (arawa, “naked, bare; open, revealed”).
スクール is borrowed from English “school”.
高い comes from the Early Middle Japanese adjective 高し (takashi).
イコール, “equal”, is borrowed from English and first cited to a text from 1901.
合う, “to fit, to match”, is from Old Japanese, and the source compares 会う (au).
